premise: I took a $130,000 reverse mortgage on my free‑and‑clear home to pay my grandson’s private‑university tuition after my son and daughter‑in‑law signed a note promising to repay me with 5% interest and provide a suite in the new house they’d build; they used my cash to construct the house, then refused me entry and said it was a gift—I sued on the note, won a $220,000 judgment, foreclosed on the house when they couldn’t satisfy the lien, and now rent rooms to college students while living in the owner’s suite, mailing them a monthly statement that grows with interest marked 'Education Costs.'
